labels.G: Guidance or possible technique; underlying outcomes can be required

media.name: W3C accessible audio and video guide

items.action: Inventory pages, routes, dialog states, and complete user journeys before review.
Record the requested features and identify missing or nonfunctional features separately.
Determine which checklist items apply to each implemented page, state, and process.
Record the browser, viewport, operating system, and assistive technologies used for testing.
Test each relevant loading, empty, success, error, and disabled state that exists.
Do not treat an untested item, missing feature, or tool error as a pass.
Consult the linked criterion and its exceptions before reporting a WCAG failure.
Involve people with disabilities and assistive-technology expertise where feasible.
Include embedded and third-party content in scope when it forms part of the experience.
Preserve original generated artifacts and record any changes made for testing.

items.section: Page structure, reading order, and language
items.action: Provide a descriptive page title for every page.

items.section: Page structure, reading order, and language
items.action: Expose the default human language of each page programmatically.

items.section: Page structure, reading order, and language
items.action: Identify changes in human language programmatically when the criterion applies.

items.section: Page structure, reading order, and language
items.action: Expose meaningful headings and the relationships they convey programmatically or in text.

items.section: Page structure, reading order, and language
items.action: Write headings and labels that describe their topic or purpose.

items.section: Page structure, reading order, and language
items.action: Make a correct reading sequence programmatically determinable when the presentation order affects meaning.

items.section: Page structure, reading order, and language
items.action: Expose meaningful list relationships programmatically or in text.

items.section: Page structure, reading order, and language
items.action: Expose meaningful group and section relationships programmatically or in text.

items.section: Page structure, reading order, and language
items.action: Provide a way to bypass repeated blocks when they appear on multiple pages.

items.section: Page structure, reading order, and language
items.action: Offer multiple ways to locate pages in a set, subject to the process exception.

items.section: Page structure, reading order, and language
items.action: Keep repeated navigation in consistent relative order unless the user changes it.

items.section: Page structure, reading order, and language
items.action: Identify components with the same functionality consistently across a set of pages.

items.section: Page structure, reading order, and language
items.action: Keep repeated help mechanisms in consistent relative order when the criterion applies.

items.section: Page structure, reading order, and language
items.action: Use native headings, lists, landmarks, and other HTML elements when they convey the intended structure.

items.section: Page structure, reading order, and language
items.action: Consider a skip link that reaches the main content when repeated navigation is present.

items.section: Page structure, reading order, and language
items.action: Avoid positive tabindex values that can make focus order difficult to maintain.
Give meaningful images an equivalent text alternative, accounting for applicable exceptions.
Give image-based controls a text alternative that communicates their purpose.
Allow decorative non-text content to be ignored by assistive technology when appropriate.
Supply equivalent information for informative charts, diagrams, and complex images.
Give non-text CAPTCHA a text alternative that identifies and describes its purpose. Provide alternatives for different sensory abilities.
Make each link purpose clear from its text or programmatically determined context, subject to the criterion exception.
Avoid instructions that rely solely on sensory characteristics such as position, shape, or sound.
Do not use color as the only visual means to convey information, actions, response prompts, or distinctions.
Use text rather than images of text when technology permits the presentation, subject to the criterion exceptions.
Include the visible text of a control in its accessible name when the criterion applies.
For an icon-only button, provide a meaningful accessible name describing its action.
Describe an informational image according to its purpose in the surrounding content.
Provide chart data in an accessible table or text summary when that gives an equivalent alternative.
Provide the required text alternative for other non-text content, accounting for the criterion exceptions.
Give an image-only link an accessible name that identifies the link purpose.

items.section: Color, contrast, layout, and display adaptation
items.action: Check normal-size text and images of normal-size text for at least 4.5:1 contrast, subject to exceptions.

items.section: Color, contrast, layout, and display adaptation
items.action: Check large text and images of large text for at least 3:1 contrast, subject to the criterion exceptions.

items.section: Color, contrast, layout, and display adaptation
items.action: Ensure visual information needed to identify controls and states has 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors. Apply the criterion exceptions.

items.section: Color, contrast, layout, and display adaptation
items.action: Check visual parts of graphics required for understanding for at least 3:1 contrast, subject to exceptions.

items.section: Color, contrast, layout, and display adaptation
items.action: Allow text to resize to 200% without assistive technology. Prevent content or function loss, subject to exceptions.

items.section: Color, contrast, layout, and display adaptation
items.action: For vertically scrolling content, avoid two-dimensional scrolling at 320 CSS pixels wide. Prevent loss of content or function, subject to exceptions.

items.section: Color, contrast, layout, and display adaptation
items.action: For horizontally scrolling content, avoid two-dimensional scrolling at 256 CSS pixels high. Prevent loss of content or function, subject to exceptions.

items.section: Color, contrast, layout, and display adaptation
items.action: Preserve content and functionality when users apply the text-spacing overrides in the criterion.

items.section: Color, contrast, layout, and display adaptation
items.action: Support portrait and landscape orientation unless a particular orientation is essential.

items.section: Color, contrast, layout, and display adaptation
items.action: When required, let users dismiss hover or focus content without moving pointer hover or keyboard focus.

items.section: Color, contrast, layout, and display adaptation
items.action: Let users move the pointer over applicable hover-triggered content without it disappearing.

items.section: Color, contrast, layout, and display adaptation
items.action: Keep applicable hover- or focus-triggered content visible until a criterion-defined dismissal condition occurs.

items.section: Color, contrast, layout, and display adaptation
items.action: Test text over images and gradients at the least-contrasting visible area.

items.section: Color, contrast, layout, and display adaptation
items.action: Use an additional shape, text, or icon to distinguish states that also use color.

items.section: Color, contrast, layout, and display adaptation
items.action: Respect the user's reduced-motion preference where motion can be reduced.

items.section: Color, contrast, layout, and display adaptation
items.action: Test the interface with browser zoom and increased text spacing.

items.section: Color, contrast, layout, and display adaptation
items.action: Check focus indicators and controls in forced-colors or high-contrast display modes.

items.section: Color, contrast, layout, and display adaptation
items.action: Check contrast in each available theme and relevant interactive state.
Make functionality operable through a keyboard interface, subject to the path-dependent exception.
Do not require specific timings for individual keystrokes, subject to the keyboard criterion exception.
Allow keyboard focus to leave any component reached by keyboard using only a keyboard interface.
Tell users the exit method when unmodified arrow, Tab, or another standard exit method is insufficient.
Preserve meaning and operability in focus order when sequence affects them.
Provide a mode where the keyboard focus indicator is visible on keyboard-operable user interfaces.
When a component receives keyboard focus, do not let author-created content entirely obscure it. Apply the criterion notes.
Allow character-only shortcuts to be disabled, remapped to include a non-printable key, or active only on focus.
For multipoint or path-based gestures, provide a single-pointer alternative without a path-based gesture, subject to exceptions.
Provide a single-pointer alternative to dragging when the dragging criterion applies.
For single-pointer functions, meet one allowed condition. Options include no execution on down-event, up-event with abort or undo, up reversal, or an essential down-event.
Provide an interface alternative to motion actuation when the criterion applies.
Allow applicable motion actuation to be disabled, subject to the criterion exceptions.
Make pointer targets at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels or satisfy an allowed exception.
Do not trigger a change of context merely when a component receives focus.
Do not automatically change context when a component's setting changes unless users receive advance notice.
Use native links for navigation and native buttons for actions where appropriate.
Check keyboard operation independently from the non-dragging pointer alternative.
Check focused elements around sticky headers, overlays, and mobile virtual keyboards.
Provide an accessible, visible close control for dismissible overlays.
Check that tab order reaches visible controls without reaching hidden controls unexpectedly.
Make keyboard focus visually distinguishable on all interactive controls.
Provide labels or instructions when a user must enter data.
Expose the relationship between a label and its input programmatically or in text.
Identify applicable input purposes programmatically for fields collecting information about the user.
Identify the input item with an automatically detected error and describe the error in text.
Suggest known corrections for detected input errors unless security or purpose would be compromised.
For covered legal or financial actions, data changes, or test responses, offer reversal, error correction, or confirmation as allowed.
Within one process, auto-populate or let users select information needed again. Include information entered by or provided to the user and apply exceptions.
Provide an allowed alternative or assistance mechanism for authentication cognitive tests, subject to exceptions.
Make form-control names and roles programmatically determinable.
Expose applicable form status messages so assistive technology can present them without focus.
Keep visible labels available after users start typing.
Indicate required fields and input format before users submit the form.
Associate field-specific error text with the affected input.
Provide an error summary linked to affected fields when a long form has several errors.
Allow password managers and pasting for authentication where feasible.
Avoid clearing correctly entered form data after a failed submission.
Make review and correction available before a significant transaction is submitted.
Expose expanded or selected states when multi-step navigation uses interactive controls.
Use appropriate autocomplete tokens for applicable personal-information fields.
Check form validation and correction with both keyboard and assistive technology.
Use clear, familiar words and explain unfamiliar terms when needed.
Make the purpose of each page and its important actions easy to identify.
Break complex instructions into clear steps.
Reduce the need to remember information across multiple steps where feasible.
Allow users to go back and correct mistakes without losing their work where feasible.
Make help or feedback options easy to find when they are provided.
Tell users about relevant costs and required information before they begin a process.
Avoid making controls or content move unexpectedly.
Expose each user-interface component's name and role programmatically.
Make user-settable component states, properties, and values programmatically settable.
Make notifications of name, role, state, property, and value changes available to user agents and assistive technologies.
Expose applicable status messages so assistive technology can present them without focus.
Preserve meaningful information and relationships conveyed through presentation in code or text.
Prefer native HTML semantics where they already provide the correct accessible behavior.
Use live regions or suitable native status semantics for applicable asynchronous status messages.
Check that live messages announce once, at an appropriate priority, with useful content.
Update accessible expanded, selected, checked, and pressed states when their controls change.
Avoid adding ARIA roles or attributes that conflict with native semantics.
Check that hidden or inactive content does not leave unexpected focusable controls available.
Check that an accessible status is understandable without surrounding visual context.
Give each dialog an accessible name that identifies its purpose.
Move focus to an appropriate location inside a modal dialog when it opens.
Keep background content inert while a true modal dialog is open.
Keep Tab and Shift+Tab within an open modal dialog.
Let users close a modal dialog with Escape when the pattern permits it.
Return focus to the invoking control after closing a dialog when it remains the logical destination.
Choose a logical focus destination if the invoking control no longer exists.
Check nested dialogs and overlays in each open and close sequence.

items.section: Menus, tabs, accordions, and carousels, when present
items.action: Distinguish ordinary site navigation from an application-style menu before choosing roles.

items.section: Menus, tabs, accordions, and carousels, when present
items.action: For application-style menus, implement the keyboard interactions for the chosen pattern.

items.section: Menus, tabs, accordions, and carousels, when present
items.action: For tabs, expose the selected tab and its associated panel.

items.section: Menus, tabs, accordions, and carousels, when present
items.action: For tabs, implement the keyboard navigation of the selected tabs pattern.

items.section: Menus, tabs, accordions, and carousels, when present
items.action: For accordions, expose whether each controlled panel is expanded or collapsed.

items.section: Menus, tabs, accordions, and carousels, when present
items.action: For accordions, make each panel trigger keyboard operable.

items.section: Menus, tabs, accordions, and carousels, when present
items.action: For carousels, provide accessible controls to move between items.

items.section: Menus, tabs, accordions, and carousels, when present
items.action: For automatically rotating carousels, provide an applicable pause or stop mechanism.

items.section: Menus, tabs, accordions, and carousels, when present
items.action: Check that closed menus and inactive panels do not expose inappropriate focus targets.

items.section: Comboboxes, listboxes, and sliders, when present
items.action: Give a combobox an accessible name and expose its expanded or collapsed state.

items.section: Comboboxes, listboxes, and sliders, when present
items.action: Connect a combobox to its popup using the semantics required by the selected pattern.

items.section: Comboboxes, listboxes, and sliders, when present
items.action: Support the selected combobox pattern's keyboard interactions, including navigation and selection.

items.section: Comboboxes, listboxes, and sliders, when present
items.action: Keep the active option available to assistive technology when focus remains on the combobox.

items.section: Comboboxes, listboxes, and sliders, when present
items.action: Preserve normal text-editing keys in an editable combobox.

items.section: Comboboxes, listboxes, and sliders, when present
items.action: Expose a custom slider's name, current value, and allowed range.

items.section: Comboboxes, listboxes, and sliders, when present
items.action: Support the keyboard interactions of the selected slider pattern.

items.section: Comboboxes, listboxes, and sliders, when present
items.action: Offer a non-dragging single-pointer way to change a slider when the criterion applies.

items.section: Comboboxes, listboxes, and sliders, when present
items.action: Verify custom widgets with actual assistive technologies, including touch where relevant.

items.section: Tables, dashboards, and data displays, when present
items.action: Make data-table headers and cell relationships programmatically determinable or available in text.

items.section: Tables, dashboards, and data displays, when present
items.action: Ensure the information conveyed by a chart has an equivalent text alternative.

items.section: Tables, dashboards, and data displays, when present
items.action: Do not use color alone to distinguish chart data or status.

items.section: Tables, dashboards, and data displays, when present
items.action: Use appropriate native table elements for tabular data.

items.section: Tables, dashboards, and data displays, when present
items.action: Associate complex table cells with the correct headers.

items.section: Tables, dashboards, and data displays, when present
items.action: Expose the current sort state on the relevant header when a table is sortable.

items.section: Tables, dashboards, and data displays, when present
items.action: Make sort and row-expansion controls keyboard operable and clearly named.

items.section: Tables, dashboards, and data displays, when present
items.action: Announce result counts or updated data when the update is an applicable status message.

items.section: Tables, dashboards, and data displays, when present
items.action: Test scrollable data regions for usable focus and reading order at narrow widths.

items.section: Tables, dashboards, and data displays, when present
items.action: Test data updates, sorting, and filtering with assistive technology in each relevant state.

items.section: Audio, video, animation, and time limits, when present
items.action: Provide an equivalent time-based media alternative for prerecorded audio-only content, subject to the criterion exception.

items.section: Audio, video, animation, and time limits, when present
items.action: Provide an equivalent time-based media alternative or audio track for prerecorded video-only content, subject to the criterion exception.

items.section: Audio, video, animation, and time limits, when present
items.action: Provide captions for prerecorded synchronized audio, subject to the stated exception.

items.section: Audio, video, animation, and time limits, when present
items.action: Provide a time-based media alternative or audio description for prerecorded video in synchronized media, subject to the criterion exception.

items.section: Audio, video, animation, and time limits, when present
items.action: Provide captions for live audio in synchronized media.

items.section: Audio, video, animation, and time limits, when present
items.action: Provide audio description for applicable prerecorded synchronized video.

items.section: Audio, video, animation, and time limits, when present
items.action: For automatic audio over three seconds, provide pause, stop, or volume control independent of the system volume.

items.section: Audio, video, animation, and time limits, when present
items.action: Provide an allowed way to turn off, adjust, or extend time limits, subject to the criterion exceptions.

items.section: Audio, video, animation, and time limits, when present
items.action: Provide pause, stop, or hide controls for applicable automatic moving, blinking, or scrolling content.

items.section: Audio, video, animation, and time limits, when present
items.action: Provide a way to pause, stop, hide, or control the frequency of applicable auto-updating information.

items.section: Audio, video, animation, and time limits, when present
items.action: Avoid more than three flashes in one second, unless flashes remain below the general and red flash thresholds.

items.section: Audio, video, animation, and time limits, when present
items.action: Provide keyboard-operable and named controls for any custom media player.

items.section: Audio, video, animation, and time limits, when present
items.action: Review captions for accuracy, speaker information, and synchronization.

items.section: Audio, video, animation, and time limits, when present
items.action: Use a transcript as an additional way to access audio or video content where feasible.

items.section: Audio, video, animation, and time limits, when present
items.action: Warn users before a timeout and preserve their entered data where feasible.
Run automated accessibility checks across the selected pages and interactive states.
Review automated findings, incomplete results, and tool errors individually.
Traverse the full flow with a keyboard and inspect visible focus.
Review semantics and announcements with suitable assistive technologies.
Inspect text alternatives, instructions, captions, and error messages for meaning.
Exercise relevant pointer, touch, motion, zoom, and display conditions.
Save reproducible steps, the affected page state, expected behavior, and observed behavior.
Link each issue to evidence and the applicable criterion or guidance.
Record pass, fail, not applicable, unassessable, or not tested with reasons.
Report missing required features separately from accessibility results.
Record tool versions and rules, reviewer experience, and test limitations.
Do not present a clean automated scan as proof of WCAG conformance.
Keep the evaluation checklist and scoring instructions out of the unchanged baseline input.
Record whether each reviewed issue comes from the generated site or an external dependency.
Keep reviewer evidence and final decisions separate from assumptions made before testing.
Keep study guidance out of the baseline runtime, including automatically loaded workspace instructions.
